column7: So, what is faith? Persuasion! The Greek word ***pistis*** means persuasion, or the result of being persuaded. We are to have persuasion towards God. In English we might say faith (persuasion) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, you hopefully have faith ‘**in’** your spouse. You believe that they will do what they said they would do, and you believe that they are being authentic and genuine. This trust should extend beyond what they’ve said, to extend to them in general.
column8: So, what is faith? Conviction! The Greek word ***pistis*** means conviction, or the result of being persuaded. We ought to have conviction toward God. In English we might say faith (conviction) ‘**in** God’. If you are married, it is hoped that you have ‘**in’** faith toward your spouse. You believe that they will do what they said they would do, and you believe that they are sincere and truthful. This confidence should not be confined only to their words, but should extend to their overall person.
